reports.title: Brali this week: knowledge quality, query access, and agent adoption
reports.summary: Brali moved beyond a large hack archive toward a smaller trusted core, problem-first topic entry points, reproducible agent evaluation, and easier zero-install access.

highlights.title: Flagship 100 trusted core
highlights.text: A deterministic quality and safety policy now selects a 100-protocol trusted core instead of treating every inherited hack as equally ready for recommendation.

highlights.title: Seven problem-first Topic Hubs
highlights.text: Sleep, Focus, Memory, Stress, Habits, Learning, and Movement now combine trusted protocols, evidence boundaries, and research-watch items in compact entry points.

highlights.title: 50-case agent evaluation suite
highlights.text: Brali added reproducible practical scenarios and later aligned the browser Query Playground with the same contract, reaching 50/50 maintained cases in the reported CI run.

highlights.title: Zero-install Query Playground
highlights.text: A browser-only surface now lets people test Brali retrieval, inspect trust and provenance, and create shareable question URLs without installing an SDK or MCP client.

highlights.title: Reference agents and MCP distribution work
highlights.text: Runnable reference-agent examples were published and the read-only Brali Knowledge MCP package was prepared for npm and MCP Registry distribution, with publication claims deliberately withheld until external publication is verified.

highlights.title: Research became a correction loop
highlights.text: Recent work narrowed claims around retrieval practice, sleep regularity, movement breaks, and habit formation instead of using research as decorative citations.

next: Turn natural-language questions into stronger internal navigation without generating one page per keyword variation.
Keep replacing inherited unsupported claims with reviewed or clearly practical protocol content.
Track search performance only when first-party Search Console data is available; do not invent search-volume or ranking trends.

reports.title: August 2026: from hack collection to evidence-aware knowledge platform
reports.summary: The August direction is consolidation: stronger quality boundaries, canonical Topics and Protocols, research decisions, machine-readable APIs, and practical ways for people and agents to retrieve the same knowledge.

highlights.title: Knowledge model
highlights.text: Canonical identity, ontology, evidence states, review queues, protocol feeds, and versioned datasets now give the library a machine-readable structure beyond individual pages.

highlights.title: Evidence boundaries
highlights.text: Selected high-risk or overclaimed inherited pages are being replaced by sourced or explicitly practical protocols, while research decisions record what a source does and does not establish.

highlights.title: Human and AI discovery
highlights.text: Topic Hubs, a Query Playground, API surfaces, integration examples, reference agents, and MCP packaging now provide several paths into the same canonical knowledge.

highlights.title: SEO direction
highlights.text: The next growth layer favors useful question-led collections, fresh reports, research notes, and internal links over mass-produced pages targeting near-identical keyword variants.

next: Expand high-value topic coverage only when the underlying trusted library can support it.
Publish a short weekly report and a month-to-date summary from verified repository and research changes.
Use Search Console query data to decide which existing hubs deserve deeper editorial pages before creating new URLs.
